paragraphs.heading: What a polynomial is
paragraphs.text: A polynomial is an expression built from variables and constants using only addition, subtraction, multiplication and raising to non-negative whole-number powers, with a finite number of terms. A simple example in one variable is x² − 4x + 7. A polynomial can use several variables at once, as in x³ + 2xyz² − yz + 1. Polynomials turn up across mathematics and science.

paragraphs.heading: Where the name comes from
paragraphs.text: The word joins the Greek poly, meaning many, with the Latin nomen, meaning name. It was formed from binomial by swapping the Latin prefix bi- for the Greek poly-. So a polynomial is a sum of many terms. The word was first used in the 17th century.

paragraphs.heading: Variable or indeterminate
paragraphs.text: The letter x goes by two names. When the polynomial is treated as an expression, x is a fixed symbol with no value, called an indeterminate. When it is treated as a function, x is the input, so it is called a variable. Many writers use the two words interchangeably. Putting a value a in place of x gives P(a), and the rule that sends a to P(a) is the polynomial function belonging to P.

paragraphs.heading: Terms, coefficients and degree
paragraphs.text: A polynomial in one indeterminate x can always be written as a_nxⁿ + aₙ₋₁xⁿ⁻¹ + ⋯ + a₂x² + a₁x + a₀, where the constants a₀ to aₙ are its coefficients. Each term is a number, its coefficient, times indeterminates raised to non-negative whole-number powers. The power on an indeterminate is its degree in that term, and adding those powers gives the degree of the term. The degree of the whole polynomial is the largest degree of any term whose coefficient is not zero.

paragraphs.heading: A worked example
paragraphs.text: Take the term −5x²y. Its coefficient is −5 and its indeterminates are x and y. Here x has degree two, and y has degree one, since a letter with no written exponent counts as power one. So the term has degree 2 + 1 = 3.

paragraphs.heading: Constants and zero
paragraphs.text: A term with no indeterminates is a constant term, and a polynomial with no indeterminates is a constant polynomial. A constant term, and any constant polynomial that is not zero, has degree 0. The zero polynomial, 0, has no terms at all, and its degree is generally left undefined.

paragraphs.heading: When two look different
paragraphs.text: Two expressions count as the same polynomial if the usual rules of commutativity, associativity and distributivity for addition and multiplication turn one into the other. So (x − 1)(x − 2) looks different from x² − 3x + 2, yet the two give one polynomial, so (x − 1)(x − 2) = x² − 3x + 2.

paragraphs.heading: What they are used for
paragraphs.text: Polynomial equations capture problems ranging from simple word problems to hard scientific ones. Polynomial functions show up in basic chemistry and physics, and in economics and social science too, and calculus and numerical analysis use polynomials to approximate other functions. In advanced mathematics they are used to build polynomial rings and algebraic varieties, which are central ideas in algebra and algebraic geometry.
